question: Should `runtimeConfig` be adopted as a supported, read-scoped gateway health JSON/RPC contract, or should this restart-pending model/provider/auth diagnostic be limited to a narrower administrator-only surface?
rationale: The implementation is additive, but it creates a durable operator-facing response shape and exposes restart-pending auth/provider state at the least-privilege health scope; source review alone cannot choose that public product boundary.

options.title: Adopt a minimal read-safe contract
options.body: Keep redacted drift state, paths, and model labels for `operator.read`, document the stable fields and sensitivity rules, then require current-head proof and green checks.

options.title: Restrict to administrator diagnostics
options.body: Expose the full drift diagnostic only through an admin-scoped health or diagnostic surface if read-scoped operational visibility is not intended as a supported API.

options.title: Defer behind config convergence work
options.body: Pause this standalone payload until the externally managed configuration work defines the broader desired-versus-applied status contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt a minimal read-safe contract
recommendation.body: Keep redacted drift state, paths, and model labels for `operator.read`, document the stable fields and sensitivity rules, then require current-head proof and green checks.

likelyOwner.reason: The related externally managed configuration direction explicitly links this PR as follow-up work and is the strongest available product-boundary signal.
